item.description: - macOS: Hotch now keeps itself up to date with Sparkle. Once a day it checks for a new version and shows the release notes with Install, Remind Me Later and Skip This Version. Check for Updates… is in Settings → App updates and the Hotch menu. - macOS: if you have Hotch 2.2.0 or 2.3.0, download this version from the release page once, as those versions cannot update themselves. Later versions arrive in the app. - macOS: an update window never appears over the welcome or during a Focus run. A line in the card says an update is available and brings the window back. - macOS: Download and install updates automatically is an opt-in in Settings. It waits until the card is closed and no Focus timer or Backpack session is running, or until you quit. - macOS: a Focus timer running when an update installs carries on in the new version. - macOS: the update check sends only the Hotch and Sparkle versions to hotch.hotherside.com and can be turned off. Sparkle's anonymous system profile is off. Sparkle is Hotch's first third-party package. - Linux: the GNOME top-bar button is back. 2.3.0 left it out of the panel, so the default top-bar home showed nothing and the card opened at the screen's left edge. Fixed by Simon (@sire6). - Linux: say when a newer Linux release is out, checking GitHub at most once a day and on demand (`hotch update-check`). A quiet line in the GNOME card footer and a tray menu item link to the release page, with **Skip this version**; Hotch never downloads or installs updates. Turn it off in Settings or with `hotch settings set updateChecks false`. Releases that change only macOS no longer attach Linux packages, so Linux users hear only about releases that change Linux. - Linux: **Check now** in Settings says when it could not check (offline, rate-limited, or no package for this machine). `hotch settings set updateSkipped` accepts `v2.4.0` as well as `2.4.0`.
